content:
maya: Quick heads-up — ran the int4 ensemble canary (raven-lite + kestrel fallback) against the prod mirror and saw structured-output (funcall) parse failures spike from ~0.9% -> 3.8%
oliver: ouch. same promptset as previous runs?
maya: same seed batch but not deterministic seed enabled for the ensemble path. replayed a few requests — failures correlate with ensemble fallback ordering (when kestrel fires after raven-lite).
sasha: do we know if it's a tokenization mismatch or serialization suffix noise?
maya: logs show partial JSON fragments where the first model writes the object close but the fallback appends a closing bracket that doesn't align, e.g. `{\"action\": \"call\", \"args\": {\"q\": 1` then fallback returns `, \"extra\": true}}` -> ends up `...1, \"extra\": true}}` which our strict parser flags.
raj: that sounds like inter-model suffix overlap. ensemble concat isn't inserting a separator. should the aggregator enforce NDJSON boundaries?
maya: I think so. Right now the ensemble concatenates raw token streams. When fallback happens mid-object, tokens from second model assume fresh context.
oliver: can we reproduce deterministically? if we lock sampling seed and mirror the ensemble ordering we might. also want to capture per-model end-of-turn sentinel tokens in traces.
infra-bot: deployment note: canary ran on dedicated_canary_2026-03-20, 60k requests, 0.38% baseline parse_err -> 3.82% canary.
sasha: short-term mitigation: wrap each model output in a one-line NDJSON record with a header that aggregator can safely join and parse. e.g. `{\"__model\":\"raven-lite\",\"body\":{...}}\n` then the aggregator tries to merge bodies with a merger that prefers first model for conflicting keys.
maya: that would avoid token-level JSON collisions. downside: changes downstream call contract and may need postprocess cost.
raj: alternative: aggregator injects a synthetic separator token (nonprinting sentinel) between streams that model can't normally emit, then strip it before parsing. might be hacky.
oliver: also we should try canary with deterministic seeds and fixed ordering to see if the problem is nondet or model behavior. if deterministic run still shows spike, it's a model-generation difference, not RNG.
sasha: I'll prototype NDJSON wrapper in the canary aggregator adapter. quick patch:```python
# aggregator postprocess pseudo
parts = [json.loads(line) for line in stream.splitlines()]
merged = {}
for p in parts:
  merged.update(p.get('body', {}))
return json.dumps(merged)
```
raj: safe but loses provenance of which model produced which field unless we keep `__model` keys.
maya: action items: 1) oliver enable deterministic_seed for 1k requests and replay (due by EOD) 2) sasha prototype NDJSON wrapper in canary aggregator (PR tomorrow) 3) raj add trace flags so per-model token boundaries are logged (small perf hit, toggleable).
oliver: doing seed replay now, will post summary in this thread.
sasha: starting a branch `canary-ndjson-merge` and will push a draft PR link when ready.
maya: thanks — if NDJSON reduces parse_err to baseline we can consider adopting as default in ensembles that touch funcalls.
oliver: one more note — add a check to eval harness that simulates mid-token fallback: cut generation at random token and append fallback output to catch regressions before canary. cheap fuzzer.
raj: agreed. also add metric to mark 'ensemble-token-boundary-collisions' so alerting can pick this up.
infra-bot: ticket created: INF-2026-378 (ensemble-parse-drift) assigned to oliver/sasha/raj, severity: P2.
maya: great. will follow up with canary logs / examples in this thread when replay finishes. :thumbsup:
